title: About the artist
quote: Art does not necessarily have to provide answers. Sometimes its main purpose is to create a space in which people can see the world and themselves anew.
paragraphs: Krystyna Mishchenko is a Ukrainian artist working in contemporary art ceramics, sculpture and visual art. Her practice explores human individuality, identity, inner freedom and the complex relationships between the individual and the surrounding world.

Academic training, the study of traditional artistic techniques and an interest in contemporary art have shaped a multifaceted practice that brings together sculptural thinking, a conceptual approach and artistic experimentation.

Ceramics occupies a central place in her work, understood not only as a material or a means of decorative expression, but above all as an independent language of artistic expression. Its sculptural, textural and spatial possibilities allow abstract ideas, emotional states and philosophical reflections to take material form.
Particular importance is placed on making the invisible tangible — giving form to memory, absence, inner contradictions and experiences that cannot be expressed through words alone.

Her artistic language is characterised by the interplay of geometric and organic structures, volume and void, colour and texture. The works often explore tensions between outward order and inner change, stability and fragility, belonging to a whole and the desire to preserve individuality. These opposites do not exist in isolation; they form an interconnected system of meanings and visual relationships.

Symbolism plays an important role. Human silhouettes, botanical motifs, geometric constructions and empty spaces become artistic metaphors through which to explore existence, memory, freedom of choice and the influence of social structures on the formation of personality. The works offer no single definitive interpretation, remaining open to individual perception.

One of the most significant strands of her practice is the creation of transformable ceramic compositions in which the artwork extends beyond a static form. The possibility of rearranging elements, creating new spatial combinations and transforming the original structure becomes integral to the artistic concept.

This approach reconsiders the traditional relationships between artwork, artist and audience. Viewers cease to be solely observers and gain the opportunity to participate directly in the artistic process. Interaction with the object becomes a form of co-creation, in which participants’ personal experiences, decisions and perceptions influence the composition’s final appearance.
Transformation becomes not only a sculptural device, but also a philosophical metaphor for human identity — changing, multifaceted and developing throughout life.

A distinct strand of artistic inquiry addresses loss, memory, isolation and inner resistance. The expressive qualities of material form reveal human vulnerability, the experience of absence and the desire to preserve one’s sense of self amid external and internal upheaval. Works created in 2022 give particular attention to war, its devastating impact on human life and the invisible traces it leaves in individual and collective memory.

Alongside conceptual sculpture, drawing, painting and decorative ceramics remain important parts of her practice. Exploring rhythm, ornament, natural structures and colour relationships develops an individual visual language that combines decorative expression with contemporary sculptural thinking.

Her professional activity encompasses artistic and teaching practice, developing creative concepts, coordinating teams and leading ceramics classes for children and adults. Experience across artistic disciplines supports an interdisciplinary approach in which traditional techniques become a foundation for exploring new forms of expression.

Her works have been presented in art and exhibition projects in Ukraine, Poland, Latvia and Finland. International artistic experience supports a dialogue between cultural traditions, individual artistic inquiry and current questions in contemporary art.

Her artistic philosophy understands art as a space for inquiry, dialogue and free interpretation. Rather than a final assertion, the artwork becomes an opportunity to ask questions, reconsider the familiar and discover new facets of one’s own perception.
